newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SETS ONE-YEAR BOND AUCTION FOR TUE. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SETS ONE-YEAR BOND AUCTION FOR TUE. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects auction date in headline and first paragraph from Wednesday.)
The Slovak Finance Ministry on Monday said it will auction an unspecified tranche of one- year state bonds on Tuesday.
The ministry said the bonds will have a fixed annual coupon of 10.00 percent and that no limit price has been set on bids.
Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters the ministry would welcome bids with yields as close as possible to the coupon.
But, he added, that "this now seemed unrealistic, due to the interbank market situation".
He would not disclose at what level the ministry would accept bids. Slovak interbank money market rates with longer maturities have been hovering at around 16 to 18 percent over the past few weeks.
In the last successful auction of one year state bonds on February 25, the ministry accepted bids worth 1.11 billion crowns, with the average yield at 14.66 percent.
